full_judgment:
5. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that on consideration and discussion of 13 PWs and 3 DWs the appellate Court came to clear findings that the plaintiffs proved the oral agreement and payment of consideration money, but the High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute without discussing a single witness of the plaintiffs and defendants and disbelieving the oral agreement and payment of consideration money. He submitted that since the suit is for specific performance of contract, the prime consideration of the Court would be whether the agreement was made and consideration was passed. Title of the defendants is immaterial. But the High Court Division erred in law in holding that when the title of the defendant is challenged the suit is not maintainable. He submitted that in an oral contract the burden of proof heavily lies upon the plaintiffs. In this case the plaintiffs examined 13 witnesses out of which PW 3 is a freedom fighter commander, PW 4 is a Senior Advocate, PW 8 is a Senior Advocate of Barguna Bar Association and lie is also 6 times elected President of Barguna Bar, PW 9 is a Senior Advocate of Barguna Bar Association and also is an elected Vice-President, PW 10 is an Ex-commissioner of Barguna Pourosova, PW 11 is an elected Chairman of Barguna Pourosova, PW 12 is the Associate Professor of Bhandaria Government Collage. They are the highly respected persons of the locality and also impartial witnesses. Those witnesses proved talk of agreement and payment of consideration money. The appellate Court as a final Court of fact on threadbare discussion relied upon the evidence of those witnesses and came to clear findings that the plaintiffs proved the oral agreement and payment of consideration money. The High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute without discussing and considering of the above evidence. He submitted that the appellate Court on discussing the evidence of PWs held that the suit is not barred by limitation, but the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the suit is barred by limitation. He submitted that the appellate Court followed the provision under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure by discussing each and every witness and reversing all the findings of the trial Court. But the High Court Division erred in law without reversing the findings of the Appellate Court and made the Rule absolute, thus dismissing the suit. He submitted that it is settled principle that the finding of facts concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court, which is the final Court of facts, is binding upon the High Court Division as revisional Court except in certain well defined exceptional circumstances such as non-consideration and misreading of material evidence on record, but the High Court Division did not mention in its judgment as to which evidence is misread and which evidence is not considered made the Rule absolute and. as such, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. 

 8. In a suit for specific performance of contract where the agreement for sale is not reduced to writing, the burden is heavily upon the plaintiff to prove by Oral evidence that there was such an agreement; that consideration money was paid and any unpaid portion of the consideration was offered; and that in spite of the offer of the remainder of the consideration amount and request to execute and register the deed of sale, the defendant refused. It is equally important that any evidence: in respect of the above is corroborated by credible independent evidence.
